description:
Walk a work's structure in order: a work gives its sections, a section its chapters, a chapter its verses (label and translation, in pages). Use it when the user wants to read a chapter or a book through, asks what comes after a verse, or what a book contains; search_texts cannot do that.

Three steps, each named in the reply of the one before: `work` alone lists the sections; add `section` for its chapters; add `chapter` (the `index` from the listing) for its verses. Every reply carries `next`, the arguments of the call that continues. To quote a verse, call get_verse with its `unit_id`: it returns the citation and version hash.

chapter.description: The chapter's `index` in the section's listing; it opens that chapter's verses.

language.description: Preferred language of the translations returned. Not a filter: works that exist only in Russian are returned in Russian, and each result says which language it is actually in. Default: en.

limit.description: Verses per page. Default 20, at most 50.

offset.description: Where in the chapter to start, counting verses from 0. Default 0.

page.description: Which page of a section's chapters. Default 1.

page_size.description: Chapters per page. Default 50, at most 100.

section.description: A section slug from the work's listing (a parva, a canto, an upaniṣad).

work.description: A work slug, as list_works gives it.

name: browse_work
title: Browse a work in order
